title: Finite scalar comparison preserves derived reduction adjuncts
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and let $R\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\xrightarrow{\psi}S$ be morphisms of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and K-flat derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$, meaning that $B\otimes_R-$ is exact, and that the multiplication map $B\otimes_R S\to S$, $b\otimes s\mapsto\psi(b)s$, is an isomorphism of sheaves.

For every $M\in D(B)$ the canonical balanced comparison is a natural isomorphism in $D(S)$,
$$\kappa_{M,S}:(\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}M)\otimes_R^L S\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_B^L S.$$
It is represented on a K-flat $B$-complex with flat terms by $x\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes s$. Give all scalar extensions their canonical derived extension--restriction adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. For every $Q\in D(S)$ and $p:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}Q$, let $p_B^\sharp:M\otimes_B^L S\to Q$ be its adjunct and let $p_R^\sharp:(\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}M)\otimes_R^L S\to Q$ be the adjunct of $\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}(p)$. Then
$$p_R^\sharp=p_B^\sharp\circ\kappa_{M,S}.$$
The comparisons commute with a morphism $S\to S'$ of $B$-algebras whenever the same multiplication-isomorphism hypothesis holds for $S'$. They also commute with successive derived scalar extensions from $S$ to $S'$ under the canonical scalar-extension associativity isomorphisms; equal-index comparison uses the canonical scalar-extension unit identification.

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Res}_{B/R}$ and let $q:P\to M$ be a flat-term K-flat $B$-resolution, supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], restriction along any of the ring maps is exact and its derived functor is termwise restriction. Thus $Uq$ is a quasi-isomorphism. We use the same underlying complex $UP$ for the $R$-side, after checking its K-flatness in the next step.

For an acyclic $R$-complex $A$, flatness of $B/R$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] make $B\otimes_R A$ acyclic. The natural cancellation of [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation], degree by degree and then on total direct sums, gives
$$\operatorname{Tot}(UP\otimes_R A)\cong U\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B(B\otimes_R A)).$$
Restriction commutes with these direct sums and detects acyclicity because the underlying abelian sheaf and its cohomology are unchanged [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The right side is acyclic by the definition of K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Hence $UP$ is K-flat. For each term the same cancellation writes $UP^i\otimes_R-$ as the composite of $B\otimes_R-$, $P^i\otimes_B-$ and exact restriction; consequently $UP^i$ is flat. This is a direct application of the cited cancellation and the definition, not a separate flat-restriction lemma.

proof.text:
Put $\mu:B\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. Cancellation [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation] followed by $1\otimes_B\mu$ gives a chain isomorphism
$$UP\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_B(B\otimes_R S)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mu}P\otimes_B S.$$
The first map sends $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes(1\otimes s)$ and its inverse sends $x\otimes(b\otimes s)$ to $bx\otimes s$. These are the sheafified balanced tensor maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. They are $S$-linear for the action on the last factor, and commute with $d_P$; all scalar factors have degree zero. The composite is $k_{P,S}(x\otimes s)=x\otimes s$. Invertibility uses exactly the assumed isomorphism $\mu$, not flatness of $S/B$.

By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $UP\otimes_R S$ and $P\otimes_B S$ represent the two derived extensions, since step 2 proves that $Uq$ is a K-flat resolution. The maps $k_{P,S}$ commute with every $B$-chain map: both composites send $x\otimes s$ to $f(x)\otimes s$. They therefore give a natural chain isomorphism on the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat $B$-complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], localization of this category at quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(B)$. The natural-transformation part of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends $k$ and its inverse uniquely, yielding the natural isomorphism $\kappa_{M,S}$ independently of the chosen resolution. This also proves naturality for derived morphisms, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms.

Let $\eta^B_M:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}(M\otimes_B^L S)$ and $\eta^R_{UM}:UM\to\operatorname{Res}_{S/R}(UM\otimes_R^L S)$ denote the canonical derived units. Their normalization in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] represents both on $P$ (respectively $UP$) by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Step 3 gives $k_{P,S}(x\otimes1)=x\otimes1$. Thus, identifying composite restriction with restriction along the composite (the scalar action is literally the composite ring map),
$$\operatorname{Res}_{S/R}(\kappa_{M,S})\circ\eta^R_{UM}=U(\eta^B_M).$$
For $M=QP$ this is the displayed chain equality. Naturality of both units and of $\kappa$ carries it along the isomorphism $Qq:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ to every $M$.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalized by derived.tex Tags 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors) and 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors).

proof.text:
The defining adjunction formula [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] sends a map $a:M\otimes_B^L S\to Q$ to $\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}(a)\circ\eta^B_M$. Accordingly, for the given arbitrary derived morphism $p$, we have $p=\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}(p_B^\sharp)\circ\eta^B_M$. The $R$-transpose of $p_B^\sharp\circ\kappa_{M,S}$ is, using step 5,
$$\operatorname{Res}_{S/R}(p_B^\sharp)\circ\operatorname{Res}_{S/R}(\kappa_{M,S})\circ\eta^R_{UM}=U(\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}(p_B^\sharp)\circ\eta^B_M)=U(p).$$
Injectivity of the $R$-adjunction bijection proves $p_R^\sharp=p_B^\sharp\circ\kappa_{M,S}$. This calculation applies to all $p\in\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(M,\operatorname{Res}_{S/B}Q)$ without requiring a chain-map representative of $p$ on the chosen $P$.

proof.text: For a morphism of $B$-algebras $\tau:S\to S'$ satisfying the second multiplication-isomorphism hypothesis, compare the square of chain maps from $UP\otimes_R S$ to $P\otimes_B S'$ formed by $k_{P,S}$, $k_{P,S'}$ and $1\otimes\tau$. Each route sends $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes\tau(s)$. These equalities hold for the actual sheaf tensor maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], since their sectionwise bilinear formulas agree before sheafification. By the K-flat computation and localization already cited in step 4 they give the asserted naturality of the derived comparisons, with the coefficient-change arrows viewed after restriction to $D(S)$.

By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], both $UP\otimes_R S$ and $P\otimes_B S$ remain flat-term K-flat over $S$. Thus they compute successive extension to $S'$ with no assumption that $S'/S$ is flat. Under the canonical associators of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], both routes from $(UP\otimes_R S)\otimes_S S'$ to $P\otimes_B S'$ send $(x\otimes s)\otimes s'$ to $x\otimes\tau(s)s'$. This proves compatibility with successive derived extension. For a further ring map $S'\to S''$ the formulas give $x\otimes\tau'(\tau(s))\tau'(s')s''$ along every parenthesization, so the comparisons agree with the iterated canonical associators. For $S'=S$ and the identity ring map, the canonical unit is $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes st$ and its inverse is $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$; hence the equal-index comparison is the canonical unit identification. The same localization argument as in step 4 carries these identities to $D(S')$.

Steps 5-6 use the unit normalization (1) for ψ and ψφ, then Hom-equivalence injectivity; this proves the adjunct equation for arbitrary derived p. Step 7 is the sectionwise square x⊗τ(s).
